detail.trustTrend: The trend number is more reliable than the daily scale reading.
detail.legend: Thick line = trend (7-day moving average), dots = daily scale readings, dashed line = goal weight. Period start and Now use the trend, not a single reading.
detail.weekly: Long ranges are averaged per week, per logged day.

status.high: Waist-to-height ratio {{ratio}}: high risk. Get your blood sugar and blood pressure checked at a clinic or doctor.
status.above: Above the healthy limit. Losing even a few cm lowers your risk.
status.below: Below the healthy limit. Keep it up.

about.title: About & how to measure
about.intro: Body weight can't tell fat from muscle. Waist size shows fat around your organs, which is most linked to diabetes and heart disease.

standard.title: Standards
standard.cutoff: Central obesity limit for Asian adults: men 90 cm, women 80 cm.
standard.ratio: Waist-to-height ratio should stay under 0.5. At a height of {{height}} cm, keep your waist under {{half}} cm.
standard.source: Sources: WHO Western Pacific (2000), Indonesian Ministry of Health, WHO Expert Consultation (2008), NICE (2022).

guide.title: How to measure
guide.step1: Stand straight, feet together, arms relaxed at your sides.
guide.step2: Find your lowest rib and the top of your hip bone. Wrap the tape exactly halfway between them.
guide.step3: Keep the tape level with the floor, snug on the skin but not squeezing.
guide.step4: Read it at the end of a normal breath out. Don't hold your breath or suck in.
guide.tip: Measure in the morning before eating. Once a week is enough.

illustration.alt: Illustration: a tape measure wrapped halfway between the lowest rib and the top of the hip bone

period.title: Period
